name: Alsace grand cru Ollwiller

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer, Riesling and Müller-Thurgau fully without cooking off their freshness.
Gewürztraminer, Riesling and Pinot Gris sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Noir is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
Faces the midday sun. In a climate this cool, that extra warmth is often what gets grapes fully ripe.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
